gaps.lead: Each gap rests on a documented absence of text, not on an assumption.
gaps.note: Each gap rests on a documented absence of text, not on an assumption.

GAP-01.title: Contrast thresholds exist. The gap moved to whether they bind.
GAP-01.finding: The 2021 Ministry of Health protocol states the eGFR < 30 threshold, the metformin categories and the risk bands, but it is practice guidance. No text was found making it binding as the dose levels are.
GAP-01.implication: Samaam cites a Saudi national protocol, and never presents it as a prohibition. It holds until an authorised person decides.
GAP-01.recommendation: A decision linking the Ministry's radiology protocols to enforcement and accountability, as Royal Decree 60057 did for the reference levels.

GAP-02.title: Liability when a tired technologist accepts an automated recommendation
GAP-02.finding: SFDA requires studying human-computer interaction (MDS-G010) and human review safeguards (MDS-G027). No text says who carries responsibility when harm occurs.
GAP-02.implication: The strongest gap in the project: a documented legislative void.
GAP-02.recommendation: A text dividing responsibility between manufacturer, facility, technologist and consultant, with a documented digital signature before any safety alert is overridden.

GAP-03.title: Reference levels bind, with no real-time enforcement
GAP-03.finding: Royal Decree 60057 and Health Council Resolution 3/88 bind providers. MDS-G008 requires automatic dose recording and periodic reports to SFDA by email.
GAP-03.implication: Enforcement is retrospective. It finds the breach after the patient was exposed.
GAP-03.recommendation: Require radiology systems to check the reference level before imaging starts, not after. This is what Samaam provides.

GAP-04.title: No cumulative dose ceiling for oncology patients
GAP-04.finding: Reference levels are set per examination. No Saudi text sets a cumulative limit for patients imaged repeatedly in oncology follow-up.
GAP-04.implication: Justification is applied scan by scan and does not see the patient's whole journey.
GAP-04.recommendation: Require cumulative dose tracking across facilities in the unified health record.

GAP-05.title: Device control is regulated more than clinical accountability
GAP-05.finding: SFDA Rule 10 places software affecting radiology devices in class C. No text requires a physician's confirmation before kVp, mAs or contrast dose change, or records liability when alerts are ignored.
GAP-05.implication: Samaam's registration path is clear. The operational governance layer is what is missing.
GAP-05.recommendation: A regulation requiring every override to be recorded and tied to the identity of the authoriser.

GAP-06.title: Data law is not medical-error law
GAP-06.finding: The PDPL implementing regulation covers transparency of automated decisions. It does not say whether clinical judgement may be delegated to an automated system, or who pays compensation.
GAP-06.implication: Relying on the PDPL alone to justify a medical system's safety is a method error.
GAP-06.recommendation: An explicit link between the data protection law and the health professions regulations.

connectors.premise: No CT scanner exposes an API to be driven through. It asks — over DICOM, at the start of a shift — for the work scheduled on it, and whoever answers decides what appears on the technologist’s screen. Samaam is that answer. The device is not modified, updated, or replaced.

notes.fhir: Read-only. Pulls the patient and their latest serum creatinine. The name, contact and address fields are never read.
notes.mwl: Samaam answers the scanner’s C-FIND itself. Every entry is evaluated first: a blocked study is not served, so it never appears in the worklist — and both outcomes are written to the audit trail.
notes.modality: Filled in by the first query that reaches the server, not typed by hand.
notes.injector: Shown on the console with the request. Nothing is sent to it while the request is held.

hero.title: A gateway between the console and the CT scanner
hero.titleAccent: that refuses what Saudi regulation forbids.
hero.lead: Samaam reads the patient's renal function, checks the scan settings against Saudi regulation, and answers 403 with the article and the issuing authority. The decision is deterministic code, not a language model.
hero.stageProtocol: The usual protocol. It looks normal on the console.
hero.riskLabel: Contrast-associated AKI risk in this band

case.title: From one keypress to a documented refusal
case.lead: An oncology patient, 62, whose chemotherapy has weakened her kidneys. A night shift, a standard adult dose, and nothing between the console and the scanner that reads her file.

arrive.title: The request arrives
arrive.body: The record carries serum creatinine of 229.8 µmol/L. The console asks for CTDIvol 18.0 mGy and DLP 900 mGy·cm.

prepare.title: Preprocessing strips and computes
prepare.body: Direct identifiers are dropped, and eGFR is computed with CKD-EPI as the Ministry of Health protocol prints it: 19.1.

check.title: The policy node checks
check.body: Four deterministic rules run, each citing its knowledge-base record by explicit ID.

refuse.title: The device refuses
refuse.body: The scanner is locked. It is a hold, not a prohibition: a named radiologist can authorise the scan, and that name goes into the audit trail.

lost.title: What gets lost in a busy shift
lost.lead: Four rules read what a tired eye misses. Each one states its basis, because a binding law and a clinical protocol are not the same thing.

paths.title: A clinical block is a hold. A privacy breach is a refusal.
paths.holdDesc: Emergencies do not wait. A named consultant may release the scan, and the release is recorded as EXECUTED_UNDER_OVERRIDE.
paths.refuseDesc: No clinician can authorise what the PDPL forbids. An export of patient records abroad ends the session, and the incident goes into the audit trail.

arch.title: If the model is deleted, every block still happens
arch.lead: The pipeline follows ITU-T Y.3172 node for node. The decision sits in P, plain rule logic. The model only writes the explanation, after the verdict has arrived.

sources.title: It speaks the language of the radiology department
sources.lead: The gateway answers a scanner's worklist query over DICOM and reads the hospital record over HL7 FHIR, read-only. Thresholds were reviewed by a consultant radiologist, which turned absolute blocks into holds for authorisation.

cta.title: The gateway is running
cta.body: Open the dashboard, load SC-02, and send it to the device. You will get a 403 with the article and the authority.
